Natural_Language: This part establishes standards for describing agency needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_100_a: Part 11 establishes standards for describing agency needs
Validation_Notes: Simple declarative scope statement. Atomic proposition is self-contained. No conditional or conjunctive structure.

Natural_Language: As used in this part- Reconditioned means restored to the original normal operating condition by readjustments and material replacement. Remanufactured means factory rebuilt to original specifications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_101: Definitions used in Part 11 consist of Reconditioned and Remanufactured
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for two definitional entries. Both definitions are operative within Part 11.

Natural_Language: Reconditioned means restored to the original normal operating condition by readjustments and material replacement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_101_a: Reconditioned means restored to original normal operating condition by readjustments and material replacement
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Establishes meaning of "reconditioned" for Part 11. No conditional or logical operator needed.

Natural_Language: Remanufactured means factory rebuilt to original specifications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_101_b: Remanufactured means factory rebuilt to original specifications
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Establishes meaning of "remanufactured" for Part 11. No conditional or logical operator needed.

Natural_Language: Policy. Agencies shall fulfill statutory requirements by specifying needs, ensuring acquisition official compliance, using metric system, allowing offeror comment, procuring sustainable products, allowing target performance levels, complying with Section 508, and not restricting telecommuting without written determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102: Policy requirements for describing agency needs
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating all seven policy subsections. All are conjunctively required as agency obligations, though (c) is advisory ("should") and (e) is permissive ("may"). The parent conjunction accurately represents that all subsections apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: In fulfilling requirements of 10 U.S.C. 3206(a), 10 U.S.C. 3453, 41 U.S.C. 3306(a), and 41 U.S.C. 3307, agencies shall specify needs using market research and ensure acquisition officials meet specified requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a: Agencies fulfill statutory requirements by specifying needs (P_11_102_a_1) and ensuring acquisition official compliance (P_11_102_a_2)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for two mandatory agency obligations under four statutory authorities. Both (1) and (2) are required. "Shall" indicates mandatory.

Natural_Language: Specify needs using market research to promote competition and limit restrictive provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_1: Agencies specify needs using market research to promote competition and limit restrictions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both promoting competition (i) and limiting restrictive provisions (ii) are required when specifying needs via market research.

Natural_Language: Only include restrictive provisions to the extent necessary to satisfy the needs of the agency or as authorized by law.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_1_ii_a: Restrictive provisions are included only to extent necessary to satisfy agency needs; P_11_102_a_1_ii_b: Restrictive provisions are authorized by law
Validation_Notes: Restrictive provisions are permissible under two disjunctive conditions: necessity for agency needs OR authorization by law. Either justification is sufficient. "Only" constrains scope but does not negate.

Natural_Language: Promote full and open competition (see part 6), or maximum practicable competition when using simplified acquisition procedures, with due regard to the nature of the supplies or services to be acquired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_1_i_a: Agency promotes full and open competition; P_11_102_a_1_i_b: Agency promotes maximum practicable competition when using simplified acquisition procedures; P_11_102_a_1_i_c: Competition is with due regard to nature of supplies or services
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive competition requirement: full and open competition OR maximum practicable competition (the latter applies when using SAP). Both alternatives are constrained by the conjunctive requirement for due regard to nature of supplies/services. The "or" is contextual, not truly optional -- which standard applies depends on acquisition method.

Natural_Language: To the maximum extent practicable, ensure that acquisition officials state requirements properly, define them for commercial products, provide competition opportunity, require commercial components, and modify requirements for commercial availability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2: Agencies ensure acquisition officials meet five requirements to maximum extent practicable
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All five sub-requirements are conjunctively required, but the introductory "to the maximum extent practicable" qualifies the entire obligation. This creates a softened mandate -- all five are required but subject to practicability. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW because the practicability qualifier introduces interpretation ambiguity.

Natural_Language: Define requirements in terms that enable and encourage offerors to supply commercial products or commercial services or, to the extent that commercial products suitable to meet the agency's needs are not available, nondevelopmental items, in response to the agency solicitations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2_ii_a: Requirements defined to enable and encourage supply of commercial products or commercial services; P_11_102_a_2_ii_b: Commercial products suitable to meet agency needs are not available; P_11_102_a_2_ii_c: Requirements defined to enable and encourage supply of nondevelopmental items
Validation_Notes: Primary obligation is to define requirements for commercial products/services. Fallback to nondevelopmental items is conditional on commercial product unavailability. The "to the extent that" phrase creates a conditional fallback. HIGH-RISK due to material implication in the fallback condition.

Natural_Language: Provide offerors of commercial products, commercial services, and nondevelopmental items an opportunity to compete in any acquisition to fill such requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2_iii_a: Offerors of commercial products are provided opportunity to compete; P_11_102_a_2_iii_b: Offerors of commercial services are provided opportunity to compete; P_11_102_a_2_iii_c: Offerors of nondevelopmental items are provided opportunity to compete
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement: all three categories of offerors must be given opportunity to compete. The "and" connecting commercial products, commercial services, and nondevelopmental items is conjunctive.

Natural_Language: Require prime contractors and subcontractors at all tiers under the agency contracts to incorporate commercial products, commercial services, or nondevelopmental items as components of items supplied to the agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2_iv_a: Prime contractors required to incorporate commercial products, commercial services, or nondevelopmental items as components; P_11_102_a_2_iv_b: Subcontractors at all tiers required to incorporate commercial products, commercial services, or nondevelopmental items as components
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement applying to both primes and subs. The types of items to incorporate (commercial products, commercial services, nondevelopmental items) are disjunctive within each atomic -- any of the three categories satisfies the component incorporation requirement.

Natural_Language: State requirements with respect to an acquisition of supplies or services in terms of- (A) Functions to be performed; (B) Performance required; or (C) Essential physical characteristics.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2_i_A: Requirements stated in terms of functions to be performed; P_11_102_a_2_i_B: Requirements stated in terms of performance required; P_11_102_a_2_i_C: Requirements stated in terms of essential physical characteristics
Validation_Notes: Explicit disjunctive list with "or" connector. Requirements may be stated using any one of three approaches: functional, performance-based, or physical characteristics. The disjunction is genuine -- any single approach satisfies.

Natural_Language: Modify requirements in appropriate cases to ensure that the requirements can be met by commercial products or commercial services or, to the extent that commercial products suitable to meet the agency's needs are not available, nondevelopmental items.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_a_2_v_a: Requirements modified to ensure they can be met by commercial products or commercial services; P_11_102_a_2_v_b: Commercial products suitable to meet agency needs are not available; P_11_102_a_2_v_c: Requirements modified to ensure they can be met by nondevelopmental items
Validation_Notes: Same conditional fallback structure as (ii). Primary obligation: modify for commercial products/services. If commercial products unavailable, modify for nondevelopmental items. "In appropriate cases" qualifier introduces discretion on when to apply. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: The Metric Conversion Act of 1975, as amended by the Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act of 1988 (15 U.S.C. 205a, et seq.), designates the metric system of measurement as the preferred system of weights and measures for United States trade and commerce, unless such use is impracticable or is likely to cause significant inefficiencies or loss of markets to United States firms.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_b_a: Metric system is the preferred system of weights and measures for US trade and commerce; P_11_102_b_b: Use of metric system is impracticable; P_11_102_b_c: Use of metric system is likely to cause significant inefficiencies or loss of markets to US firms
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Metric system is default preference with two exception conditions. "Unless" creates a conditional: metric is preferred when neither impracticability nor significant inefficiency/market loss applies. The exceptions are disjunctive -- either one alone is sufficient to override the metric preference. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with negated antecedent.

Natural_Language: To the extent practicable and consistent with subpart 9.5, potential offerors should be given an opportunity to comment on agency requirements or to recommend application and tailoring of requirements documents and alternative approaches. Requiring agencies should apply specifications, standards, and related documents initially for guidance only, making final decisions on the application and tailoring of these documents as a product of the design and development process. Requiring agencies should not dictate detailed design solutions prematurely (see 7.101 and 7.105(a)(8)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_c_a: Potential offerors given opportunity to comment on agency requirements or recommend tailoring; P_11_102_c_b: Requiring agencies apply specifications and standards initially for guidance only; P_11_102_c_c: Requiring agencies do not dictate detailed design solutions prematurely
Validation_Notes: Advisory requirement using "should" throughout. Three recommended practices are conjunctively stated. Not binding but represents best practice guidance. "To the extent practicable and consistent with subpart 9.5" qualifies the first recommendation. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW per advisory "should" override rule.

Natural_Language: Agencies shall procure sustainable products in accordance with subpart 23.1, and unless exceptions apply, shall incorporate sustainable products when developing specifications, describing requirements, and developing source-selection factors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d: Sustainable product procurement and incorporation requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the general procurement mandate (1) and the specific incorporation requirements (2) are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Agencies shall procure sustainable products in accordance with subpart 23.1.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d_1_a: Agencies procure sustainable products in accordance with subpart 23.1
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ("shall"). Direct obligation to procure sustainable products per subpart 23.1 requirements. Atomic proposition is self-contained.

Natural_Language: Unless it is not practicable (see 23.102(a)) or an exception or exemption applies (see 23.105 and 23.106, respectively), agencies shall incorporate the use of sustainable products when developing, reviewing, or revising specifications; describing Government requirements; and developing source-selection factors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d_2: Agencies incorporate sustainable products in three specified activities unless exceptions apply
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate. "Unless" creates exception conditions (impracticability per 23.102(a), exceptions per 23.105, exemptions per 23.106). When no exception applies, all three incorporation activities are conjunctively required. P_11_102_d_2_exc represents the combined exception/exemption condition. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with negated antecedent.

Natural_Language: Describing Government requirements for products and services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d_2_ii: Agencies incorporate sustainable products when describing Government requirements for products and services
Validation_Notes: Sub-element of conditional mandate. Activity trigger: describing Government requirements for products and services.

Natural_Language: Developing source-selection factors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d_2_iii: Agencies incorporate sustainable products when developing source-selection factors
Validation_Notes: Sub-element of conditional mandate. Activity trigger: developing source-selection factors.

Natural_Language: Developing, reviewing, or revising Federal and military specifications, product descriptions (including commercial item descriptions) and standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_d_2_i: Agencies incorporate sustainable products when developing, reviewing, or revising Federal and military specifications, product descriptions, and standards
Validation_Notes: Sub-element of conditional mandate. Activity trigger: any development, review, or revision of specifications, product descriptions, or standards. The "or" between developing/reviewing/revising is disjunctive -- any single activity triggers the requirement.

Natural_Language: Some or all of the performance levels or performance specifications in a solicitation may be identified as targets rather than as fixed or minimum requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_e_a: Performance levels or performance specifications are identified as targets rather than fixed or minimum requirements
Validation_Notes: Permissive "may" creates discretionary authority. Agencies have the option but not the obligation to designate performance levels as targets. Tautological consequent represents unrestricted choice. The "some or all" qualifier further broadens discretion on scope of application.

Natural_Language: In accordance with section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d), the contracting officer shall obtain from the requiring activity the requirement documents, which must identify the needs of users with disabilities, applicable ICT accessibility standards, and any standards that cannot be met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f: Contracting officer obtains requirement documents identifying disability needs, ICT accessibility standards, and exceptions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. "Shall" makes this mandatory. Requirement documents must identify three categories of information conjunctively. The statutory authority (Section 508) is the legal basis.

Natural_Language: The needs of current and future users with disabilities to determine how users with disabilities will perform the functions supported by the ICT and how the ICT will be developed, installed, configured and maintained to support users with disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f_1: Requirement documents identify needs of current and future users with disabilities
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both aspects (how users perform functions, how ICT supports users) must be addressed conjunctively.

Natural_Language: The ICT will be developed, installed, configured and maintained to support users with disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f_1_ii_a: ICT developed to support users with disabilities; P_11_102_f_1_ii_b: ICT installed to support users with disabilities; P_11_102_f_1_ii_c: ICT configured to support users with disabilities; P_11_102_f_1_ii_d: ICT maintained to support users with disabilities
Validation_Notes: Four lifecycle phases of ICT support for disabled users are conjunctively required. "And" connector between developed, installed, configured, and maintained makes all four mandatory.

Natural_Language: Users with disabilities will perform the functions supported by the information and communication technology (ICT).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f_1_i: Requirement documents identify how users with disabilities will perform functions supported by ICT
Validation_Notes: Sub-element identifying how disabled users will interact with ICT functionality. Atomic, no further decomposition needed.

Natural_Language: The applicable ICT accessibility standards (see subpart 39.2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f_2: Requirement documents identify applicable ICT accessibility standards per subpart 39.2
Validation_Notes: Mandatory identification of applicable ICT accessibility standards. Cross-reference to subpart 39.2 for standard definitions.

Natural_Language: Any ICT accessibility standards that cannot be met due to an exception or an exemption for any component or portion of the product (see 7.105(b)(5)(iv), 39.204, and 39.205).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_f_3_a: ICT accessibility standards cannot be met due to exception; P_11_102_f_3_b: ICT accessibility standards cannot be met due to exemption
Validation_Notes: Conditional identification requirement. When any ICT accessibility standard cannot be met (due to either exception or exemption), requirement documents must identify it. The trigger is disjunctive (exception OR exemption). Cross-references to 7.105(b)(5)(iv), 39.204, and 39.205 for exception/exemption criteria. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Agencies shall not include in a solicitation a requirement that prohibits an offeror from allowing its employees to telecommute unless the contracting officer executes a written determination in accordance with FAR 7.108(a).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_102_g_a: Agency includes in solicitation a requirement prohibiting offeror from allowing employee telecommuting; P_11_102_g_b: Contracting officer executes written determination in accordance with FAR 7.108(a)
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception. Default: agencies shall not include anti-telecommute provisions. Exception: permitted only when CO executes written determination per 7.108(a). "Unless" creates conditional exception. Logically: absence of written determination implies prohibition on anti-telecommute requirement. Equivalently: anti-telecommute requirement implies written determination exists. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with negation.

Natural_Language: In accordance with OMB Circular A-119, "Federal Participation in the Development and Use of Voluntary Consensus Standards and in Conformity Assessment Activities," and Section 12(d) of the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act of 1995, Pub. L. 104-113 (15 U.S.C. 272 note), agencies must use voluntary consensus standards, when they exist, in lieu of Government-unique standards, except where inconsistent with law or otherwise impractical.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_201_a: Voluntary consensus standards exist; P_11_201_b: Agencies use voluntary consensus standards in lieu of Government-unique standards; P_11_201_c: Use of voluntary consensus standards is inconsistent with law; P_11_201_d: Use of voluntary consensus standards is impractical
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate. Three conjunctive conditions must hold for the obligation to apply: (1) voluntary consensus standards exist, (2) use is not inconsistent with law, (3) use is not impractical. "Must" makes this mandatory when conditions are met. "Except where" creates negated exception conditions. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with multiple conditions.

Natural_Language: Agencies shall select existing requirements documents or develop new requirements documents that meet the needs of the agency in accordance with the guidance contained in the Federal Standardization Manual, FSPM-0001; for DoD components, DoD Manual 4120.24, Defense Standardization Program (DSP) Procedures; and for IT standards and guidance, the Federal Information Processing Standards Publications (FIPS PUBS).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_202_a: Agencies select existing requirements documents or develop new ones meeting agency needs; P_11_202_b: Requirements documents conform to Federal Standardization Manual FSPM-0001; P_11_202_c: DoD components conform to DoD Manual 4120.24; P_11_202_d: IT standards conform to FIPS PUBS
Validation_Notes: Mandatory obligation ("shall"). Three guidance sources apply contextually: FSPM-0001 is universal, DoD Manual 4120.24 applies only to DoD, FIPS PUBS applies only to IT. The structure is conjunctive for the general obligation but the specific guidance sources are contextually disjunctive based on agency and subject matter. Flagged for review due to complexity in guidance source applicability.

Natural_Language: Market acceptance. Head of agency may require market acceptance demonstration, and contracting officer shall ensure criteria meet specified standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203: Market acceptance requirements and criteria
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Subsection (a) establishes permissive authority for market acceptance demonstration; subsection (b) establishes mandatory criteria standards.

Natural_Language: 41 U.S.C. 3307(e) provides that, in accordance with agency procedures, the head of an agency may, under appropriate circumstances, require offerors to demonstrate that the items offered have achieved market acceptance or been satisfactorily supplied, and otherwise meet solicitation criteria.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_a: Head of agency may require offerors to demonstrate market acceptance
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ("may") for head of agency. Both conditions (1) and (2) must be demonstrated conjunctively when the authority is exercised. "Under appropriate circumstances" further qualifies discretion. Flagged for review because "may" creates discretionary authority but the sub-requirements are mandatory when exercised.

Natural_Language: Have either achieved commercial market acceptance or been satisfactorily supplied to an agency under current or recent contracts for the same or similar requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_a_1: Items have achieved market acceptance or been satisfactorily supplied
Validation_Notes: Explicit disjunction with "either...or". Offerors can satisfy by demonstrating market acceptance OR satisfactory prior supply. Either pathway is sufficient.

Natural_Language: Been satisfactorily supplied to an agency under current or recent contracts for the same or similar requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_a_1_ii: Items offered have been satisfactorily supplied to an agency under current or recent contracts for same or similar requirements
Validation_Notes: Atomic proposition. Alternative pathway to market acceptance. "Current or recent" introduces temporal flexibility. "Same or similar" introduces scope flexibility.

Natural_Language: Achieved commercial market acceptance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_a_1_i: Items offered have achieved commercial market acceptance
Validation_Notes: Atomic proposition. One of two disjunctive pathways for demonstrating item acceptability.

Natural_Language: Otherwise meet the item description, specifications, or other criteria prescribed in the public notice and solicitation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_a_2: Items otherwise meet item description, specifications, or other criteria in public notice and solicitation
Validation_Notes: Additional requirement beyond market acceptance demonstration. Items must also meet solicitation criteria. This is conjunctive with (1) -- both market acceptance AND solicitation compliance are needed.

Natural_Language: In developing criteria for demonstrating that an item has achieved commercial market acceptance, the contracting officer shall ensure the criteria in the solicitation reflect minimum need and consider the entire relevant commercial market.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_b: Contracting officer ensures market acceptance criteria meet specified standards
Validation_Notes: Mandatory obligation ("shall"). Both criteria requirements are conjunctively required when developing market acceptance demonstration criteria.

Natural_Language: Reflect the minimum need of the agency and are reasonably related to the demonstration of an item's acceptability to meet the agency's minimum need.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_b_1_a: Criteria reflect minimum need of the agency; P_11_203_b_1_b: Criteria are reasonably related to demonstration of item acceptability to meet minimum need
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement: criteria must both reflect minimum need AND be reasonably related to demonstrating acceptability. "And" connector makes both mandatory.

Natural_Language: Consider the entire relevant commercial market, including small business concerns.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_203_b_2_a: Criteria consider entire relevant commercial market; P_11_203_b_2_b: Criteria consider small business concerns
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement. "Including" explicitly adds small business concerns to the broader market consideration, making both mandatory. The "including" reinforces that small business is a subset that must be explicitly addressed.

Natural_Language: Agency requirements shall not be written to require a particular brand name, product, or a feature of a product, peculiar to one manufacturer, thereby precluding consideration of a product manufactured by another company, unless specified conditions are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204: Prohibition on brand-name requirements with conditions for exception
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. The base prohibition applies universally. Subsections (a), (b), and (c) specify the conditions under which brand-name requirements are permissible and cross-references for specific contract types.

Natural_Language: Unless the brand name is essential and market research supports it, authority for limited competition exists, and documentation is posted for acquisitions over $25,000.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a: Three conditions for brand-name exception
Validation_Notes: All three conditions must be met conjunctively for the brand-name exception to apply. These operate as an "unless" clause to the general prohibition in the intro text.

Natural_Language: The particular brand name, product, or feature is essential to the Government's requirements, and market research indicates other companies' similar products, or products lacking the particular feature, do not meet the agency's needs or cannot be modified to meet the agency's minimum needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a_1_a: Brand name, product, or feature is essential to Government requirements; P_11_204_a_1_b: Market research indicates other companies similar products do not meet agency needs or cannot be modified to meet minimum needs
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement: both essentiality AND market research support are needed. Neither alone is sufficient. Market research must affirmatively show alternatives are inadequate or unmodifiable.

Natural_Language: The authority to contract without providing for full and open competition is supported by justifications and approvals, or the basis for limited competition is documented for simplified acquisition procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a_2: Authority for limited competition is properly supported
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive requirement. Two alternative pathways for establishing authority: formal J&A under 6.302-1 OR simplified acquisition documentation. Which applies depends on the acquisition method.

Natural_Language: The basis for not providing for maximum practicable competition is documented in the file (see 13.106-1(b)) or justified (see 13.501) when the acquisition is awarded using simplified acquisition procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a_2_ii_a: Basis for limited competition documented in file per 13.106-1(b); P_11_204_a_2_ii_b: Basis for limited competition justified per 13.501; P_11_204_a_2_ii_c: Acquisition awarded using simplified acquisition procedures
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement triggered by SAP usage. When SAP is used, either file documentation per 13.106-1(b) OR justification per 13.501 is sufficient. The "or" is genuinely disjunctive. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: The authority to contract without providing for full and open competition is supported by the required justifications and approvals (see 6.302-1).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a_2_i: Authority to contract without full and open competition supported by J&A per 6.302-1
Validation_Notes: Atomic proposition. Requires formal justification and approval per FAR 6.302-1 for sole source or limited competition.

Natural_Language: The documentation or justification is posted for acquisitions over $25,000. (See 5.102(a)(6).)
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_a_3_a: Acquisition value exceeds $25,000; P_11_204_a_3_b: Documentation or justification is posted
Validation_Notes: Conditional posting requirement triggered by dollar threshold. When acquisition exceeds $25,000, posting is mandatory. Below threshold, no posting requirement. Cross-reference to 5.102(a)(6) for posting procedures. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: For multiple award schedule orders, see 8.405-6.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_b: Multiple award schedule orders subject to 8.405-6
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference provision directing to 8.405-6 for brand-name rules specific to MAS orders. No substantive requirement beyond the reference.

Natural_Language: For orders under indefinite-quantity contracts, see 16.505(a)(4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_204_c: Indefinite-quantity contract orders subject to 16.505(a)(4)
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference provision directing to 16.505(a)(4) for brand-name rules specific to IDIQ orders. No substantive requirement beyond the reference.

Natural_Language: Policy on acceptable material. Agencies must require identification of used, reconditioned, or remanufactured supplies and may require additional information on recovered material standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301: Acceptable material identification and information requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the identification requirements (a) and additional information provisions (b) apply.

Natural_Language: Identification requirements for used, reconditioned, or remanufactured supplies in both non-commercial and commercial product acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_a: Supply identification requirements for non-commercial and commercial products
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Separate rules apply for non-commercial products (1) and commercial products (2).

Natural_Language: When acquiring products other than commercial products as defined in 2.101, agencies must require offerors to identify used, reconditioned, or remanufactured supplies; or unused former Government surplus property proposed for use under the contract. These supplies or property may not be used in contract performance unless authorized by the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_a_1_a: Acquisition is for products other than commercial products as defined in 2.101; P_11_301_a_1_b: Agencies require offerors to identify used, reconditioned, remanufactured supplies or unused former Government surplus property; P_11_301_a_1_c: Supplies or property may not be used unless authorized by contracting officer
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate triggered by non-commercial acquisition. "Must" makes identification mandatory. Second sentence adds a prohibition: identified supplies cannot be used without CO authorization, creating a default-deny posture. Both the identification requirement and the use restriction are conjunctively required. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: When acquiring commercial products, the contracting officer must consider the customary practices in the industry for the product being acquired. The contracting officer may require offerors to provide information on used, reconditioned, or remanufactured supplies, or unused former Government surplus property proposed for use under the contract. The request for the information must be included in the solicitation, and to the maximum extent practicable must be limited to information or standards consistent with normal commercial practices.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_a_2_a: Acquisition is for commercial products; P_11_301_a_2_b: CO considers customary industry practices; P_11_301_a_2_c: CO may require offerors to provide information on used/reconditioned/remanufactured supplies; P_11_301_a_2_d: Information request included in solicitation; P_11_301_a_2_e: Information request limited to extent practicable to normal commercial practices
Validation_Notes: Nested conditional. When acquiring commercial products: (1) CO must consider industry practices (mandatory), (2) CO may require additional info (permissive), but (3) if CO does require info, it must be in the solicitation and limited to commercial practices. The "may" for the information request creates discretion, but exercising that discretion triggers mandatory constraints. HIGH-RISK due to nested material implications.

Natural_Language: Additional information requirements for recovered material and biobased standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_b: Additional information and biobased product requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the general additional information authority (1) and the biobased product limitation (2) apply.

Natural_Language: When the contracting officer needs additional information to determine whether supplies meet minimum recovered material or biobased standards stated in the solicitation, the contracting officer may require offerors to submit additional information on the recycled or biobased content or related standards. The request for the information must be included in the solicitation. When acquiring commercial products, limit the information to the maximum extent practicable to that available under normal commercial practices.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_b_1_a: CO needs additional info to determine compliance with recovered material or biobased standards; P_11_301_b_1_b: CO may require offerors to submit additional information; P_11_301_b_1_c: Request included in solicitation; P_11_301_b_1_d: For commercial products, info limited to normal commercial practices
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Conditional permissive authority with constraints. Trigger: CO needs additional info. "May" creates discretion on requiring submission. If discretion exercised, solicitation inclusion is mandatory and commercial product limitation applies. Tautological representation of "may" combined with conditional constraints on exercise. HIGH-RISK due to nested implications.

Natural_Language: For biobased products, agencies may not require, as a condition of purchase of such products, the vendor or manufacturer to provide more data than would typically be provided by other business entities offering products for sale to the agency, other than data confirming the biobased content of a product (see 7 CFR 3201.8).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_301_b_2_a: Agency requires vendor to provide data exceeding typical commercial data as condition of purchase; P_11_301_b_2_b: Data required is confirming biobased content
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with carve-out. Agencies cannot demand excessive data from biobased product vendors, EXCEPT for data confirming biobased content. The "other than" creates an exception to the prohibition. Logically: if the requested data is not biobased content confirmation, then excessive data requirements are prohibited. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with negation.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.211-5, Material Requirements, in solicitations and contracts for supplies that are not commercial products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_302_a: Supplies are not commercial products; P_11_302_b: Clause 52.211-5 Material Requirements inserted in solicitations and contracts
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion requirement. Trigger: non-commercial product supply acquisition. Consequence: mandatory insertion of 52.211-5. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Scope. This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for liquidated damages and specifies exclusions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400: Scope of liquidated damages subpart
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the affirmative scope (a) and the exclusions (b) define the subpart boundaries.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for using liquidated damages clauses in solicitations and contracts for supplies, services, research and development, and construction.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400_a: Subpart 11.4 prescribes policies and procedures for liquidated damages clauses in solicitations and contracts for supplies, services, R&D, and construction
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Establishes applicability to four contract types: supplies, services, R&D, construction.

Natural_Language: This subpart does not apply to liquidated damages for subcontracting plans, Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards, or paid sick leave.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400_b: Exclusions from subpart 11.4 applicability
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for three conjunctive exclusions. All three categories are excluded from this subpart.

Natural_Language: For subcontracting plans (see 19.109).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400_b_1: Liquidated damages for subcontracting plans excluded from subpart 11.4
Validation_Notes: Exclusion. Subcontracting plan LD governed by 19.109 instead.

Natural_Language: Related to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards statute (see subpart 22.3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400_b_2: Liquidated damages related to Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards excluded from subpart 11.4
Validation_Notes: Exclusion. CWHSS liquidated damages governed by subpart 22.3 instead.

Natural_Language: Related to paid sick leave for Federal contractors (see subpart 22.21).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_400_b_3: Liquidated damages related to paid sick leave excluded from subpart 11.4
Validation_Notes: Exclusion. Paid sick leave LD governed by subpart 22.21 instead.

Natural_Language: Policy on liquidated damages. CO must consider impact before using LD, LD are compensatory not punitive, CO must mitigate, and agency head may reduce or waive.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401: Liquidated damages policy requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Four conjunctive policy elements govern LD usage.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must consider the potential impact on pricing, competition, and contract administration before using a liquidated damages clause. Use liquidated damages clauses only when the time of delivery is so important that damage is expected from delinquency, and the extent of damage would be difficult or impossible to estimate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_a: CO must consider impacts and use LD only when two conditions are met
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both conditions must be met conjunctively ("and") for LD clause use to be appropriate. "Only when" restricts usage to these specific circumstances.

Natural_Language: The time of delivery or timely performance is so important that the Government may reasonably expect to suffer damage if the delivery or performance is delinquent.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_a_1_a: Time of delivery or timely performance is critically important; P_11_401_a_1_b: Government may reasonably expect to suffer damage from delinquent delivery or performance
Validation_Notes: First condition for LD use. Both the importance of timing and the reasonable expectation of damage are required. These are conceptually linked but both must be established.

Natural_Language: The extent or amount of such damage would be difficult or impossible to estimate accurately or prove.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_a_2_a: Extent or amount of damage would be difficult to estimate accurately or prove; P_11_401_a_2_b: Extent or amount of damage would be impossible to estimate accurately or prove
Validation_Notes: Second condition for LD use. Disjunctive: damage estimation is either difficult OR impossible. Either threshold satisfies the condition.

Natural_Language: Liquidated damages are not punitive and are not negative performance incentives (see 16.403-2). Liquidated damages are used to compensate the Government for probable damages. Therefore, the liquidated damages rate must be a reasonable forecast of just compensation for the harm that is caused by late delivery or untimely performance of the particular contract. Use a maximum amount or a maximum period for assessing liquidated damages if these limits reflect the maximum probable damage to the Government. Also, the contracting officer may use more than one liquidated damages rate when the contracting officer expects the probable damage to the Government to change over the contract period of performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_b_a: LD are not punitive and not negative performance incentives; P_11_401_b_b: LD rate is a reasonable forecast of just compensation for harm from late delivery/performance; P_11_401_b_c: Maximum amount or period used if reflecting maximum probable damage; P_11_401_b_d: CO may use more than one LD rate when probable damage changes over performance period
Validation_Notes: Complex policy statement combining mandatory requirements with discretionary elements. Non-punitive nature (a) and reasonable forecast requirement (b) are mandatory. Maximum cap (c) is conditional ("if these limits reflect"). Multiple rate authority (d) is permissive ("may"). Tautological representation for permissive/conditional elements.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must take all reasonable steps to mitigate liquidated damages. If the contract contains a liquidated damages clause and the contracting officer is considering terminating the contract for default, the contracting officer should seek expeditiously to obtain performance by the contractor or terminate the contract and repurchase (see subpart 49.4). Prompt contracting officer action will prevent excessive loss to defaulting contractors and protect the interests of the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_c_a: CO takes all reasonable steps to mitigate liquidated damages; P_11_401_c_b: Contract contains LD clause and CO considers T4D; P_11_401_c_c: CO seeks expeditiously to obtain performance or terminate and repurchase
Validation_Notes: Two-part requirement. First: mandatory mitigation obligation ("must"). Second: conditional recommendation ("should") when LD clause exists and T4D is being considered, CO should pursue performance or reprocure. Second sentence uses advisory "should" but is combined with mandatory first sentence. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency may reduce or waive the amount of liquidated damages assessed under a contract, if the Commissioner, Financial Management Service, or designee approves (see Treasury Order 145-10).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_401_d_a: Head of agency reduces or waives LD amount; P_11_401_d_b: Commissioner, Financial Management Service, or designee approves
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ("may") with prerequisite. FMS Commissioner approval is necessary for agency head to exercise reduction/waiver discretion. Even with approval, "may" means agency head retains discretion on whether to reduce/waive. Tautological consequent represents unrestricted choice given the prerequisite.

Natural_Language: Procedures for liquidated damages. Include LD clause and rates in solicitations, and describe construction LD rates.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_402: Liquidated damages procedural requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both general solicitation requirements (a) and construction-specific requirements (b) apply.

Natural_Language: Include the applicable liquidated damages clause and liquidated damages rates in solicitations when the contract will contain liquidated damages provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_402_a_a: Contract will contain liquidated damages provisions; P_11_402_a_b: Applicable LD clause included in solicitation; P_11_402_a_c: LD rates included in solicitation
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement. When contract will have LD provisions, both the clause and the rates must be in the solicitation. Conjunctive: both elements required, not just one. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Construction contracts with liquidated damages provisions must describe the rate(s) of liquidated damages assessed per day of delay. The rate(s) should include estimated daily cost of Government inspection and superintendence and other expected expenses.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_402_b: Construction contract LD rate description requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for construction LD rates. The "must describe" is mandatory. The "should include" for cost components is advisory. The examples (b)(1) and (b)(2) are illustrative of "other expected expenses." Flagged because parent mixes mandatory and advisory language.

Natural_Language: Renting substitute property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_402_b_1: Renting substitute property is an expected expense associated with delayed completion
Validation_Notes: Example of additional expected expense for LD rate calculation in construction. Listed under advisory "should" with "such as" framing, making it illustrative rather than mandatory.

Natural_Language: Paying additional allowance for living quarters.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_402_b_2: Paying additional allowance for living quarters is an expected expense associated with delayed completion
Validation_Notes: Example of additional expected expense for LD rate calculation in construction. Listed under advisory "should" with "such as" framing, making it illustrative rather than mandatory.

Natural_Language: Contract clauses for liquidated damages. Three clause provisions for different contract types.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_403: Liquidated damages contract clause requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Three clause provisions apply to different contract types. All three rules are operative simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Use the clause at 52.211-11, Liquidated Damages-Supplies, Services, or Research and Development, in fixed-price solicitations and contracts for supplies, services, or research and development when the contracting officer determines that liquidated damages are appropriate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_403_a_a: Contract is fixed-price for supplies, services, or R&D; P_11_403_a_b: CO determines LD are appropriate; P_11_403_a_c: Clause 52.211-11 inserted
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion. Both conditions (fixed-price contract type AND CO determination of appropriateness) must be met. When both hold, 52.211-11 insertion is mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Use the clause at 52.211-12, Liquidated Damages-Construction, in solicitations and contracts for construction, other than cost-plus-fixed-fee, when the contracting officer determines that liquidated damages are appropriate. If the contract specifies more than one completion date for separate parts or stages of the work, revise paragraph (a) of the clause to state the amount of liquidated damages for delay of each separate part or stage of the work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_403_b_a: Contract is for construction other than CPFF; P_11_403_b_b: CO determines LD are appropriate; P_11_403_b_c: Clause 52.211-12 inserted; P_11_403_b_d: Contract specifies more than one completion date; P_11_403_b_e: Paragraph (a) of clause revised for each part/stage
Validation_Notes: Nested conditional. Outer: construction (non-CPFF) + CO determination triggers 52.211-12 insertion. Inner: if multiple completion dates exist, clause must be revised for each stage. CPFF explicitly excluded. HIGH-RISK due to nested material implications.

Natural_Language: Use the clause at 52.211-13, Time Extensions, in solicitations and contracts for construction that use the clause at 52.211-12, Liquidated Damages-Construction, when that clause has been revised as provided in paragraph (b) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_403_c_a: Construction contract uses clause 52.211-12; P_11_403_c_b: Clause 52.211-12 has been revised per paragraph (b); P_11_403_c_c: Clause 52.211-13 Time Extensions inserted
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion dependent on prior clause usage and revision. Both 52.211-12 presence AND its revision per (b) are required to trigger 52.211-13 insertion. Creates a chain dependency: 11.403(b) revision triggers 11.403(c) insertion. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: This subpart implements the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS), a Department of Commerce regulation in support of approved national defense, emergency preparedness, and energy programs (see 15 CFR part 700).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_500_a: Subpart 11.5 implements DPAS; P_11_500_b: DPAS is a Department of Commerce regulation supporting approved national defense, emergency preparedness, and energy programs
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement establishing this subpart as the FAR implementation of the DPAS regulation at 15 CFR part 700.

Natural_Language: As used in this subpart- Approved program, Delegate Agency, National defense, and Rated order are defined.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_501: Definitions used in subpart 11.5
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for four definitional entries. All four definitions are operative within subpart 11.5.

Natural_Language: Approved program means a program determined in writing as necessary or appropriate for priorities and allocations support to promote the national defense by the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Energy, or the Secretary of Homeland Security, under the authority of the Defense Production Act and Executive Order 13603, or the Selective Service Act and Executive Order 12742.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_501_a: Approved program is a program determined in writing as necessary or appropriate for priorities and allocations support by SecDef, SecEnergy, or SecDHS under DPA/EO 13603 or SSA/EO 12742
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Three officials may make the determination (disjunctive) under two alternative legal authorities (disjunctive). The "necessary or appropriate" standard is itself disjunctive.

Natural_Language: Delegate Agency means a Government agency authorized by delegation from the Department of Commerce to place priority ratings on contracts or orders needed to support approved programs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_501_b: Delegate Agency is a Government agency authorized by Commerce delegation to place priority ratings on contracts/orders supporting approved programs
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Establishes that Delegate Agencies derive authority from Commerce Department delegation.

Natural_Language: National defense means programs for military and energy production or construction, military or critical infrastructure assistance to any foreign nation, homeland security, stockpiling, space, and any directly related activity. Such term includes emergency preparedness activities conducted pursuant to Title VI of The Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.) and critical infrastructure protection and restoration (50 U.S.C. 4552).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_501_c: National defense encompasses military/energy production, foreign assistance, homeland security, stockpiling, space, related activities, emergency preparedness, and critical infrastructure
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Broad definition encompassing multiple program categories. "Includes" indicates non-exhaustive list expanded by statutory reference.

Natural_Language: Rated order means a prime contract, a subcontract, or a purchase order in support of an approved program issued in accordance with the provisions of the DPAS regulation (15 CFR part 700).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_501_d: Rated order is a prime contract, subcontract, or purchase order supporting an approved program issued per DPAS regulation
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Three disjunctive instrument types (prime, sub, PO) all qualify when supporting approved programs per DPAS.

Natural_Language: General. Presidential authority under the Defense Production Act and delegation to Secretary of Commerce.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_502: General DPAS authority and delegation
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the underlying presidential authority (a) and the delegation structure (b) establish the legal framework.

Natural_Language: Under Title I of the Defense Production Act of 1950 (50 U.S.C. 4501), the President is authorized to require preferential acceptance and performance of contracts and orders supporting certain approved national defense and energy programs and to allocate materials, services, and facilities in such a manner as to promote these approved programs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_502_a_a: President authorized to require preferential acceptance and performance of contracts supporting approved programs; P_11_502_a_b: President authorized to allocate materials, services, and facilities to promote approved programs
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive presidential authorities under DPA Title I: (1) require preferential acceptance/performance, and (2) allocate resources. Both powers exist simultaneously.

Natural_Language: The President delegated the priorities and allocations authorities of the Defense Production Act in Executive Order 13603. As part of that delegation, the President designated the Secretary of Commerce to administer the DPAS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_502_b_a: President delegated DPA priorities and allocations authorities via EO 13603; P_11_502_b_b: Secretary of Commerce designated to administer DPAS
Validation_Notes: Declarative statement establishing delegation chain. Both the delegation and the Commerce designation are factual statements of existing authority structure.

Natural_Language: DPAS procedures covering priority levels, Delegate Agency authority, rated order placement, compliance, guidance, CO procedures, special priorities assistance, Commerce enforcement, and violation reporting.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503: DPAS procedural requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Nine conjunctive procedural requirements spanning priority levels, authorities, placement, compliance, guidance, procedures, assistance, enforcement, and reporting.

Natural_Language: There are two levels of priority for rated orders established by the DPAS, identified by the rating symbols "DO" and "DX". All DO rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over unrated orders. All DX rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over DO rated and unrated orders (see 15 CFR 700.11). The DPAS regulation contains provisions concerning the elements of a rated order (see 15 CFR 700.12); acceptance and rejection of rated orders (see 15 CFR 700.13); preferential scheduling (see 15 CFR 700.14); extension of priority ratings (flowdown) (see 15 CFR 700.15); changes or cancellations of priority ratings and rated orders (see 15 CFR 700.16); use of rated orders (see 15 CFR 700.17); and limitations on placing rated orders (see 15 CFR 700.18).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_a_a: DO rated orders have equal priority and preference over unrated orders; P_11_503_a_b: DX rated orders have equal priority and preference over DO and unrated orders; P_11_503_a_c: DPAS regulation at 15 CFR 700.11-700.18 contains detailed provisions
Validation_Notes: Descriptive statement establishing the two-tier priority system. DO < DX in priority. Both take preference over unrated. Cross-references to 15 CFR 700.11-700.18 for detailed DPAS provisions.

Natural_Language: The Delegate Agencies have been given authority by the Department of Commerce to place rated orders in support of approved programs (see Schedule I of the DPAS). Other U.S. Government agencies, Canada, and foreign nations may apply for priority rating authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_b_a: Delegate Agencies have Commerce authority to place rated orders for approved programs; P_11_503_b_b: Other US agencies, Canada, and foreign nations may apply for priority rating authority
Validation_Notes: First sentence is declarative establishing existing Delegate Agency authority. Second sentence uses "may apply" creating permissive authority for other entities. Tautological representation for the permissive element.

Natural_Language: Rated orders shall be placed in accordance with the provisions of the DPAS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_c: Rated orders placed in accordance with DPAS provisions
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ("shall"). All rated orders must comply with DPAS provisions. Simple, unambiguous directive.

Natural_Language: Agency heads shall ensure compliance with the DPAS by contracting activities within their agencies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_d: Agency heads ensure DPAS compliance by their contracting activities
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ("shall"). Places compliance oversight responsibility on agency heads for their contracting activities.

Natural_Language: Agency heads shall provide contracting activities with specific guidance on the issuance of rated orders in support of approved agency programs, including the general limitations and jurisdictional limitations on placing rated orders (see 15 CFR 700.18 and Executive Order 13603).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_e_a: Agency heads provide specific guidance on rated order issuance; P_11_503_e_b: Guidance includes general and jurisdictional limitations on placing rated orders
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ("shall"). Agency heads must both provide guidance AND include limitation information. "Including" makes the limitations a mandatory element of the guidance.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers shall follow agency procedural instructions concerning the use of rated orders in support of approved agency programs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_f: Contracting officers follow agency procedural instructions for rated orders
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ("shall"). COs must follow their agency-specific procedures for rated orders. Creates a flow-down from 11.503(e) agency head guidance to CO-level compliance.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers, contractors, or subcontractors at any tier, that experience difficulty placing rated orders, obtaining timely delivery under rated orders, locating a contractor or supplier to fill a rated order, ensuring that rated orders receive preferential treatment by contractors or suppliers, or require rating authority for items not automatically ratable under the DPAS, should promptly seek special priorities assistance in accordance with agency procedures (see 15 CFR 700.50-700.55 and 700.80).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_g_a: COs, contractors, or subcontractors experience difficulty with rated orders or require non-automatic rating authority; P_11_503_g_b: Special priorities assistance sought promptly per agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Advisory conditional ("should"). When difficulties arise with rated orders (five enumerated scenarios), prompt pursuit of special priorities assistance is recommended. "Should" makes this advisory rather than mandatory, but the implication structure is correct. Multiple trigger conditions are disjunctive (any difficulty type triggers the recommendation). HIGH-RISK due to material implication. Flagged also for advisory "should."

Natural_Language: The Department of Commerce may take specific official actions (Ratings Authorizations, Directives, Letters of Understanding, Administrative Subpoenas, Demands for Information, and Inspection Authorizations) to implement or enforce the provisions of the DPAS (see 15 CFR 700.60-700.71).
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_h: Department of Commerce may take official enforcement actions under DPAS
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ("may") for Commerce Department. Six enumerated action types available. Tautological representation reflects discretionary nature of enforcement. Flagged for review because "may" creates discretion.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers shall report promptly any violations of the DPAS in accordance with agency procedures to the Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security, U.S. Department of Commerce, Room 3876, Washington, DC 20230, Ref: DPAS; telephone: (202) 482-3634 or email DPAS@bis.doc.gov.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_503_i_a: CO identifies DPAS violation; P_11_503_i_b: CO reports violation promptly per agency procedures to Commerce OSIS
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement ("shall"). When violations are identified, prompt reporting is mandatory. Contact information specifies the reporting destination. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provision and contract clause requirements for rated orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_504: DPAS solicitation provision and contract clause requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both the solicitation provision (a) and the contract clause (b) are required for rated orders.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers shall insert the provision at 52.211-14, Notice of Priority Rating for National Defense, Emergency Preparedness, and Energy Program Use, in solicitations when the contract to be awarded will be a rated order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_504_a_a: Contract to be awarded will be a rated order; P_11_504_a_b: Provision 52.211-14 inserted in solicitation
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion ("shall"). When contract will be a rated order, 52.211-14 provision is mandatory in the solicitation. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers shall insert the clause at 52.211-15, Defense Priority and Allocation Requirements, in contracts that are rated orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_11_504_b_a: Contract is a rated order; P_11_504_b_b: Clause 52.211-15 inserted in contract
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion ("shall"). When contract is a rated order, 52.211-15 clause is mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.
